```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(knitr)
  library(readr)
})
root <- normalizePath('../..', winslash = '/', mustWork = TRUE)
out <- file.path(root, 'output', 'bleaching_only_dhw_binomial')
comparison <- read_csv(file.path(out, 'paired_comparison.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
folds <- read_csv(file.path(out, 'fold_metrics.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
coverage <- read_csv(file.path(out, 'coverage.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
shape <- read_csv(file.path(out, 'event_shape_comparison.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
coefficients <- read_csv(file.path(out, 'event_coefficients.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
focal_contrasts <- read_csv(file.path(out, 'focal_2016_2024_probability_contrasts.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
labels <- c(
  apparent_full_data = 'Apparent full-data fit',
  leave_one_event_out = 'Leave one event out',
  leave_one_sector_out = 'Leave one sector out',
  reef_blocked_5fold = 'Pooled reef-blocked 5-fold',
  leave_one_programme_out = 'Leave one programme out'
)
round_numeric <- function(data, digits = 3) {
  data |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, digits)))
}
```

## Result

The local-first logger adjustment does **not** provide a generally transferable
improvement for this deliberately simple DHW-only occurrence model. It improves
pooled leave-one-event-out Brier score from
`r sprintf('%.4f', comparison$brier_raw_noaa_dhw[comparison$scheme == 'leave_one_event_out'])`
to
`r sprintf('%.4f', comparison$brier_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw[comparison$scheme == 'leave_one_event_out'])`,
but discrimination remains below chance (AUC approximately
`r sprintf('%.3f', comparison$auc_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw[comparison$scheme == 'leave_one_event_out'])`).
The adjustment worsens reef-blocked, sector-held-out and
programme-held-out Brier score. Raw NOAA DHW is therefore the more stable
standalone predictor; local-first DHW remains a supported exposure correction,
not evidence that DHW alone explains bleaching mortality.

The event-specific fits show that the adjustment can materially change the
apparent response shape. Slopes flatten in 2016, 2017 and 2024 and change sign
in 2020 and 2022. Those curves are descriptive full-event fits with sparse
positive outcomes in some years, so the differences identify sensitivity to
the exposure representation rather than stable event-specific mechanisms.
There is no validated 2025 correction layer: its raw and adjusted event curve
is intentionally identical, while its held-out prediction can still differ
because the two models learn different slopes from 2016--2024.

## Estimand and eligibility

The response is whether harmonised relative mortality is greater than zero.
This is a genuine Bernoulli regression; the mortality proportions are not
converted into invented colony counts. Each model contains only an intercept
and one linear DHW term on the logit scale.

"Bleaching-compatible" follows the selected thermal-component contract. Rows
explicitly marked as COTS, cyclone or flood affected are excluded. Explicitly
bleaching-labelled rows and rows with no explicit non-thermal attribution are
retained; the latter are shown in the audit rather than silently called
confirmed bleaching. The May--April event window and post-May mortality cutoff
are unchanged.

```{r}
coverage |>
  select(
    event_year, observations, reefs, mortality_occurrences,
    explicit_bleaching_rows, unlabelled_compatible_rows,
    nonzero_corrections, nonzero_correction_fraction,
    raw_dhw_min, raw_dhw_max, adjusted_dhw_min, adjusted_dhw_max
  ) |>
  round_numeric() |>
  kable(caption = 'Eligible observations and local-first correction coverage.')
```

## Predictive comparisons

The apparent fit is included only as a calibration diagnostic. Leave-one-event
out tests transfer to an unseen bleaching event. Leaving out a sector tests
geographic transfer; the pooled reef-blocked split keeps every observation
from a reef in the same fold even when that reef occurs in multiple programmes;
and leaving out a programme tests transfer across observation systems.

```{r}
comparison |>
  transmute(
    Validation = unname(labels[scheme]),
    `Raw Brier` = brier_raw_noaa_dhw,
    `Adjusted Brier` = brier_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw,
    `Adjusted minus raw` = delta_brier_adjusted_minus_raw,
    `Raw log loss` = log_loss_raw_noaa_dhw,
    `Adjusted log loss` = log_loss_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw,
    `Raw AUC` = auc_raw_noaa_dhw,
    `Adjusted AUC` = auc_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw
  ) |>
  round_numeric(4) |>
  kable(caption = 'Paired predictive performance; lower Brier and log loss are better.')
```

### Event transfer

```{r}
folds |>
  filter(scheme == 'leave_one_event_out') |>
  select(fold, variant, n, observed_occurrence, predicted_occurrence, brier, log_loss, auc) |>
  mutate(
    variant = recode(
      variant,
      raw_noaa_dhw = 'Raw NOAA DHW',
      local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw = 'Logger-adjusted DHW'
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(as.integer(fold), variant) |>
  round_numeric(4) |>
  kable(caption = 'Leave-one-event-out performance by held-out event.')
```

### Sector transfer

```{r}
folds |>
  filter(scheme == 'leave_one_sector_out') |>
  select(fold, variant, n, observed_occurrence, predicted_occurrence, brier, auc) |>
  mutate(
    variant = recode(
      variant,
      raw_noaa_dhw = 'Raw NOAA DHW',
      local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw = 'Logger-adjusted DHW'
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(fold, variant) |>
  round_numeric(4) |>
  kable(caption = 'Leave-one-sector-out performance. Very small sectors are descriptive only.')
```

## Does logger adjustment alter event curve shape?

### Focal comparison: 2016 and 2024

![](../../output/bleaching_only_dhw_binomial/focal_2016_2024_curves.png)

The two focal events give the clearest evidence that local correction changes
the fitted curve, but not in a uniform way.

In 2016, raw NOAA DHW has a slope of
`r sprintf('%.3f', coefficients$dhw_slope[coefficients$event_year == 2016 & coefficients$variant == 'raw_noaa_dhw'])`
per DHW on the logit scale (95% Wald interval
`r sprintf('%.3f to %.3f', coefficients$dhw_slope_lower95[coefficients$event_year == 2016 & coefficients$variant == 'raw_noaa_dhw'], coefficients$dhw_slope_upper95[coefficients$event_year == 2016 & coefficients$variant == 'raw_noaa_dhw'])`).
The adjusted slope is only
`r sprintf('%.3f', coefficients$dhw_slope[coefficients$event_year == 2016 & coefficients$variant == 'local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw'])`
and its interval crosses zero. At 8 DHW, the fitted probability falls from
`r sprintf('%.3f', focal_contrasts$predicted_probability_raw_noaa_dhw[focal_contrasts$event_year == 2016 & focal_contrasts$dhw == 8])`
to
`r sprintf('%.3f', focal_contrasts$predicted_probability_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw[focal_contrasts$event_year == 2016 & focal_contrasts$dhw == 8])`.
The adjustment is nonzero for 22 of 30 rows and is mostly positive (median
`r sprintf('%+.2f', coverage$correction_median[coverage$event_year == 2016])`
DHW), which moves many observations rightward and weakens the slope.

In 2024, both slopes remain positive, but adjustment reduces the slope from
`r sprintf('%.3f', coefficients$dhw_slope[coefficients$event_year == 2024 & coefficients$variant == 'raw_noaa_dhw'])`
to
`r sprintf('%.3f', coefficients$dhw_slope[coefficients$event_year == 2024 & coefficients$variant == 'local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw'])`,
a reduction of about
`r scales::percent(1 - coefficients$dhw_slope[coefficients$event_year == 2024 & coefficients$variant == 'local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw'] / coefficients$dhw_slope[coefficients$event_year == 2024 & coefficients$variant == 'raw_noaa_dhw'], accuracy = 1)`.
Corrections are nonzero for 150 of 181 rows and are mostly negative (median
`r sprintf('%+.2f', coverage$correction_median[coverage$event_year == 2024])`
DHW; 10th--90th percentile
`r sprintf('%+.2f to %+.2f', coverage$correction_q10[coverage$event_year == 2024], coverage$correction_q90[coverage$event_year == 2024])`).
The adjusted curve is therefore higher at 4 DHW, similar near 8 DHW, and lower
at 12 DHW: it primarily flattens the fitted contrast across the exposure
range.

```{r}
coefficients |>
  filter(event_year %in% c(2016, 2024)) |>
  transmute(
    event_year,
    DHW = recode(
      variant,
      raw_noaa_dhw = 'Raw NOAA',
      local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw = 'Logger adjusted'
    ),
    n, mortality_occurrences, correction_coverage,
    slope = dhw_slope,
    lower95 = dhw_slope_lower95,
    upper95 = dhw_slope_upper95,
    p_value = dhw_slope_p_value,
    odds_ratio_per_DHW = odds_ratio_per_dhw,
    fitted_probability_050_DHW = probability_050_dhw
  ) |>
  round_numeric(3) |>
  kable(caption = 'Focal event-specific slope estimates and uncertainty.')
```

The event-held-out comparison is less favourable than the descriptive curve
change alone suggests. For 2016 the adjustment worsens Brier score and AUC.
For 2024 it slightly improves Brier score by raising the very low mean
prediction toward the high observed occurrence, while AUC falls. Thus the
2024 gain is mainly calibration, not better reef ranking.

```{r}
folds |>
  filter(
    scheme == 'leave_one_event_out',
    fold %in% c('2016', '2024')
  ) |>
  transmute(
    event_year = fold,
    DHW = recode(
      variant,
      raw_noaa_dhw = 'Raw NOAA',
      local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw = 'Logger adjusted'
    ),
    n, observed_occurrence, predicted_occurrence, brier, log_loss, auc
  ) |>
  arrange(event_year, DHW) |>
  round_numeric(4) |>
  kable(caption = 'Focal leave-one-event-out predictive performance.')
```

```{r}
focal_contrasts |>
  select(
    event_year, dhw,
    raw_probability = predicted_probability_raw_noaa_dhw,
    adjusted_probability = predicted_probability_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw,
    delta_probability_adjusted_minus_raw
  ) |>
  round_numeric(3) |>
  kable(caption = 'Fitted focal-event probability at common model-input DHW values.')
```

### All six event curves

![](../../output/bleaching_only_dhw_binomial/event_specific_curves.png)

Both lines in each panel come from separate binomial fits using only that
event. They are plotted against the DHW value supplied to each model, not as a
claim that adjusted and raw DHW are interchangeable physical scales. Shading
is the model-based 95% interval; extrapolation beyond each event's observed
DHW range should not be interpreted.

```{r}
shape |>
  transmute(
    event_year,
    observations = n_raw_noaa_dhw,
    mortality_occurrences = mortality_occurrences_raw_noaa_dhw,
    correction_coverage = correction_coverage_raw_noaa_dhw,
    raw_slope = dhw_slope_raw_noaa_dhw,
    adjusted_slope = dhw_slope_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw,
    slope_change = delta_slope_adjusted_minus_raw,
    raw_midpoint_dhw = probability_050_dhw_raw_noaa_dhw,
    adjusted_midpoint_dhw = probability_050_dhw_local_first_logger_adjusted_dhw
  ) |>
  round_numeric(3) |>
  kable(caption = 'Event-specific response-shape comparison on the logit scale.')
```

## Interpretation limits

- A positive mortality occurrence is not the same as severe mortality; this
  analysis does not model positive magnitude.
- The local-first correction is spatially uneven. A slope change can reflect
  which reefs have logger support as well as a better estimate of heat stress.
- The event-specific curves reuse their event outcomes and are explanatory;
  only the held-out rows measure transfer.
- The 2025 assessment is locked against pre-2025 outcome training, but there is
  no validated 2025 logger correction. Zero adjustment is explicit, not an
  assertion that NOAA had zero bias.
- This diagnostic cannot promote a production model. It isolates what one heat
  predictor can and cannot explain after obvious non-thermal confounding is
  removed.

## Reproduction

```text
Rscript src/evaluation/test_bleaching_only_dhw_binomial.R
quarto render analysis/investigations/bleaching_only_dhw_binomial_assessment.qmd
```
